name: Persian and Iranian Studies
description: Recognizes undergraduates who combine the study of Persian language and literature with wider engagement with the art, philosophy, religion, history, politics, and culture of the Persian-speaking world.
notes: Students must attend three events (e.g. Iran Colloquium lectures, Persian Circle, Persian-language film screenings, PSA events, CMES/NELC/SASC/CAI events) and submit a 1–2 page write-up for each.
All courses must be taken for a letter grade of B or above.
Only two content courses should originate in the same department.
Persian L5 courses are content-oriented and may count as either a content or language course.
Premodern Iranian language courses (e.g. Old Persian, Middle Persian, Soghdian) count as content courses.
No course taken Credit/D/Fail may be applied toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Graduate and professional school courses may count toward the certificate.
Courses taken at another institution or during an approved summer or term-time study abroad program may count with DUS approval.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.

nonCourseRequirements: Attend three approved Persian and Iranian studies events and submit a 1 to 2 page write-up about each to the certificate director
policy.sourceNote: No more than two course credits fulfilling the requirements of the Persian and Iranian Studies Certificate may overlap with a major, a simultaneous degree, or another certificate. Courses are drawn from a list of approved courses and must be taken for a letter grade of B or above.

requirements.name: Content courses
requirements.description: Three courses with YC Persia & Iran Content attribute covering art, philosophy, religion, history, politics, and culture of the Persian-speaking world.
